name: Voltage transformer set with broken-delta residual winding
summary: Three single-phase VTs whose residual windings are connected in broken delta to produce the zero-sequence voltage.
description: In this arrangement three single-phase earthed VTs each carry a residual winding, and the three residual windings are connected in series as a broken delta. In a healthy balanced system the voltage across the open corner is near zero, and during an earth fault it rises towards three times the zero-sequence voltage, which feeds residual voltage and directional earth-fault elements.

A damping resistor is often connected across the broken delta to suppress ferroresonance in isolated or resonant-earthed networks. The symbol does not show that resistor or the earthing of the VT primaries, both of which need explicit detail on the schematic.
readingNotes: Check the primaries are earthed star so zero sequence can be measured.
Look for a damping resistor across the open corner.
distinction: A broken-delta winding measures residual voltage; an open-delta (V-V) connection measures line voltages with two VTs.
